statement: Price sensitivity differs by category: FOODS demand responds most to price (within-series elasticity -0.51) and HOUSEHOLD least (-0.35).
test: Feature ablation step 4 (+price) gives the largest WRMSSE gain in FOODS; SHAP price attributions are largest in FOODS.

statement: Most series are intermittent: 98% of HOBBIES and 87% of FOODS series are intermittent or lumpy (Syntetos–Boylan).
test: Croston/TSB beat ETS on intermittent/lumpy series; a Tweedie or Poisson LightGBM objective beats L2 on them.

statement: All categories have a strong weekly cycle peaking at the weekend; peak/trough ratio ranges from 1.37 (FOODS) to 1.48 (HOUSEHOLD).
test: Seasonal naive (7) beats naive (1) at every horizon; calendar features give a material gain in ablation step 2.

statement: SNAP days lift FOODS more than HOUSEHOLD in every state (FOODS/HOUSEHOLD SNAP ratio-of-ratios 1.064–1.254).
test: Ablation step 3 (+SNAP) improves FOODS WRMSSE but not HOUSEHOLD/HOBBIES.

statement: 20,731 series contain 50,900 implausible 14–55-day zero runs (2.97% of active series-days), consistent with unobserved stockouts; a further 11.30% of active series-days sit in dormant runs of 56+ days, which are kept as real demand regimes.
test: Headline metrics are re-run with these days masked (spec §2.1); model rankings should not change.

statement: Demand trends upward 2011–2015 in every category (CAGR 7.4%–17.3%), partly through assortment growth (new items entering)
test: Models with level adaptation (ETS, rolling features) beat long-window averages; bias stays near zero on the test window.
